html:
Virginia planter, lawyer and thinker, the main author of the Declaration of Independence and the third president of the United States, from 1801 to 1809.

In 1776 he wrote that "all men are created equal" with rights to "life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness". He later served as minister to France, as the first secretary of state and as vice president.

As president he bought the vast Louisiana territory from Napoleon in 1803, the Louisiana Purchase, which doubled the country's size. He sent the Lewis and Clark expedition to explore it. He also signed the law that banned bringing enslaved people into the country from 1808.

He enslaved more than 600 people in his lifetime and freed only a few. Most historians accept that he fathered children with Sally Hemings, an enslaved woman at his home, Monticello.

In old age he founded the University of Virginia. He died on 4 July 1826, fifty years to the day after the Declaration, a few hours before his old rival and friend John Adams.
sum: Virginia planter, lawyer and thinker, the main author of the Declaration of Independence and the third president of the United States, from 1801 to 1809.
